metadata.note: Q1bv 3m: balanced equation H₂SO₄(aq) + 2NaOH(aq) → Na₂SO₄(aq) + 2H₂O(l). Q1bvi 2m: n(H₂SO₄) = c×V = (4.9/98) × (25.0/1000) = 0.05 × 0.025 = 1.25×10⁻³ mol. Q1bvii 3m: M(Na₂SO₄)=142 g/mol; mass = 1.25×10⁻³ × 142 = 0.1775 g ≈ 0.18 g. H₂SO₄ concentration = 4.9 g/dm³.

question.name: CSEC Chem Jan 2023 Q1b(v/vi/vii) — Balanced Equation, Moles, and Mass of Na₂SO₄
question.text:
Dilute sulfuric acid (concentration: 4.9 g dm⁻³) was titrated against sodium hydroxide solution. The concordant titre was 25.0 cm³ of H₂SO₄.

(v) Write a balanced equation, including state symbols, for the formation of the normal salt from sulfuric acid and sodium hydroxide. (3 marks)

(vi) Calculate the number of moles of sulfuric acid used to neutralize the sodium hydroxide. (Molar mass: H₂SO₄ = 98 g mol⁻¹) (2 marks)

(vii) Calculate the mass of the normal salt (Na₂SO₄) expected from the reaction. (R.A.M.: Na = 23, O = 16, S = 32) (3 marks)
question.general_feedback:
Q1b(v) — Balanced equation:

H₂SO₄(aq) + 2NaOH(aq) → Na₂SO₄(aq) + 2H₂O(l)

Normal salt = sodium sulfate (Na₂SO₄). State symbols: (aq) for solutions, (l) for liquid water.

Q1b(vi) — Moles of H₂SO₄:

Concentration = 4.9 g dm⁻³ ÷ 98 g mol⁻¹ = 0.05 mol dm⁻³

n = c × V = 0.05 × (25.0/1000) = 0.05 × 0.025 = 1.25 × 10⁻³ mol

Q1b(vii) — Mass of Na₂SO₄:

From equation: n(Na₂SO₄) = n(H₂SO₄) = 1.25 × 10⁻³ mol (1:1 molar ratio)

M(Na₂SO₄) = 2(23) + 32 + 4(16) = 46 + 32 + 64 = 142 g mol⁻¹

mass = n × M = 1.25 × 10⁻³ × 142 = 0.1775 g ≈ 0.178 g

fields.label: Balanced equation: _____
fields.diagnostic_hint: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. 2 moles of NaOH needed per mole of H₂SO₄ (diprotic acid). State symbols: (aq) for both reactants and Na₂SO₄; (l) for water.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: Sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄) is a diprotic acid — it provides 2 H⁺ ions, so 2 moles of NaOH are needed to neutralize 1 mole of H₂SO₄. Balanced: H₂SO₄(aq) + 2NaOH(aq) → Na₂SO₄(aq) + 2H₂O(l).

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: Convert g dm⁻³ to mol dm⁻³: divide by molar mass. c = 4.9 ÷ 98 = 0.05 mol dm⁻³.

fields.label: Moles of H₂SO₄ = _____ mol
fields.diagnostic_hint: n = c × V = 0.05 mol dm⁻³ × 0.025 dm³ = 1.25 × 10⁻³ mol

error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: Use n = c × V. Convert volume to dm³ first: 25.0 cm³ = 0.025 dm³.

error_codes.SC_METHOD_ERROR: From the equation, the molar ratio of H₂SO₄ : Na₂SO₄ = 1:1, so n(Na₂SO₄) = n(H₂SO₄) = 1.25×10⁻³ mol.
